correctness.rationale: The exact triple-convolution expression is derived by Fubini and differentiated elementary convolutions. Its denominator cannot vanish for a>b>0. The large-Doppler rational expansion has a negative real leading term and purely imaginary 1/w correction; convexity gives a unique transverse positive limiting delay. A two-real-variable analytic IFT proves one high-frequency root per sufficiently large half-integer phase, the O(n^-2)/O(n^-1) location laws, and Doppler simplicity; Lambert-W inversion gives the close-rate divergence. The actual packaged checker independently verified symbolic identities and numerical integral/root test cases.

value.rationale: Mixed-polarity order-three exponential convolutions are a structurally natural next case after established two-factor zero-free results. The theorem supplies a genuine infinite real ambiguity-zero family, a sharp limiting-delay equation, precise Doppler density and a singular coalescing-rate delay scale, rather than a routine parameter substitution or isolated numerical example.
